8
Related Work

8.1
Staged Computation

Typed languages with staging constructs,
such as MetaML
[
67
,
69
,
68
]

or
\lambda^{\bigcirc}

[
16
,
17
]
,
arose from the context of partial evaluation
[
51
,
28
,
29
]
,
and a considerable amount of studies
have been done subsequently
[
15
,
26
,
66
,
9
,
77
,
72
,
32
,
42
]
.
Although they differ from one another in
the design choice of constructs,
many of them aim at ensuring the validity of produced code
statically by checking code-generating programs.
As to implementation,
BER MetaOCaml
[
44
,
45
]

extends OCaml with MetaML-style staging constructs,
and Scala 3
[
63
]

recently adopted a staging-based formalization for the core of its macro system.

Combining staging with types dependent on values in some sense
seems to be investigated by somewhat limited number of studies.
Concoqtion
[
24
]
has
both indexed types and staging constructs,
but their use is for establishing a tagless staged interpreter
[
53
]
,
and the language for computation and that for indices are separated.
Kawata and Igarashi
[
42
]
propose

\lambda^{\mathrm{MD}}
,
a dependently-typed multi-stage language that can be regarded as a theoretical foundation.
It also supports a kind of cross-stage persistence
based on
\lambda^{\triangleright\%}

[
32
]
.
Unlike our staged core language,

\lambda^{\mathrm{MD}}
does not have some mechanism like
stage-
0
assertions
\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(\!\!\!\;|}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\triangleleft}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}|\!)}}^{L}
,
and its type equality for checking function applications is based on the
\beta
-equivalence.

8.2
Tensor Shape Checking

Checking the consistency of programs as to tensor shapes is also a classical topic.
The incorporation of length-indexed vector types into realistic languages
dates back at least to Dependent ML
[
74
,
75
]
,
and handling data-independent sizes of structures as type-level information
has already been targeted by
shapely types

[
40
]
.
Since then, a variety of studies have been done to design a mechanism
that is less general than full dependent types but handier in some sense
for major use cases of tensor computation.

Repa
[
43
]

uses some kind of shape information at type level
and supports
shape polymorphism

[
59
]
,
i.e., the ability to reuse functions for some class of the shapes,
by exploiting usual type classes,

associated data types

[
11
]
,
and
type families

[
60
]

offered by GHC
[
71
]
.
Its main purpose of the use is, however, to achieve high-performance tensor computation
while keeping high-level description in source programs at the same time,
and seems not to pursue the complete elimination of shape mismatches.
Accelerate
[
12
]

follows a Repa-based interface for its frontend of GPGPU programs.
It also performs dynamic code generation for producing GPU kernel functions,
so the utilization of our staging-based formalization
for systems like Accelerate might be worth investigating.

To achieve strict safety, Gibbons
[
27
]
proposes
an elegant embedded-DSL approach to
checking shape consistency as to operations similar to those of APL
[
39
,
37
]

by using
Naperian
functors, type classes,
and the extension of GHC
[
71
]
for dependent types.
This also supports
rank polymorphism
,
a mechanism to allow conversions close to
broadcasting
[
19
,
14
]
.
To support realistic programs, however,
it would be good if tensor shapes are more “first-class,”
as pointed out in Hattori et al.
[
33
]
.
Henriksen and Elsman
[
34
]

and Bailly et al.
[
6
]

give another interesting formalization
mainly for the use in Futhark
[
35
]
:
a system with
size-dependent types
.
While it may cause runtime errors due to array indexing or
runtime coercion,
it allows term-level variables for type-level indices and
accommodates dynamically determined shapes by existential quantification on indices.
Somewhat similar mechanisms are also proposed by
Abe and Sumii
[
1
]
and Xi
[
75
]
,
the former of which exploits
phantom types
in OCaml.
It might be worth considering to combine our work with such existential quantification
to achieve better handling of tensors with dynamic shapes.

As another line of work, those based on
refinement types
[
25
,
23
,
58
,
46
]

or manifest contracts
[
22
,
73
,
30
,
31
,
61
]

are also prominent.
Some early researches, such as
hybrid type checking (
\lambda^{\mathrm{H}}
)
[
23
,
46
]

or liquid types
[
58
]
,
already mention array bounds checking as one of their applications.
GraTen
[
33
]
propels this approach forward
to support many tensor-related operations used in realistic DNN-related programs,
such as examples of
ocaml-torch

[
10
]
,
with a flavor of gradual typing
[
62
]
.
Migeed, Reed, Ansel, and Palsberg
[
49
]
propose
a less expressive gradually-typed system
in order to strike a balance between the coverage of the verification
and the affinity with the existing tool support.
Our use of refinement types for stage-
0
types is highly inspired by that of GraTen,
although we provide shape-related functions like
broadcast
just as literally usual functions
while GraTen handles them carefully so that the back-end SMT solver can ensure subtyping relations.

8.3
Bidirectional Type-Checking for Implicit Arguments

The idea of utilizing bidirectional type-checking
[
21
]

for reconstructing implicit arguments is not very new;
Odersky et al.
[
52
]

give such a formalization as a foundation of Scala 3’s
\mathbf{implicit}
-parameters.
Due to the dependent nature of our formalization, however,
we have found that
extending Xie and Oliveira’s “let arguments go first”
[
76
]

better fits our purpose.

8.4
Distinction between Compile Time and Runtime

Although ours seems to give a staging-based foundation for tensor shape checking
with a mathematical safety guarantee for the first time,
the distinction between data available only at compile time (e.g., parameters for matrix sizes)
and those at runtime (e.g., matrices themselves) by some other forms
appears to have long been done by a number of existing studies.
In particular, Idris 2
[
8
]
,
which has a quite different core language from the previous version of Idris
[
7
]
,
adopts
quantitative type theory
(
QTT
)
[
48
,
5
]

for distinguishing the two.
Investigating the relationship
between QTT-based type systems and staging-based ones,
such as interoperability,
might be another interesting topic.
Other than that, LMS-Verify
[
2
]

proposes a method somewhat similar to ours from the operational perspective
and provides an example of how to check size consistency of matrix operations,
based on
lightweight modular staging
(
LMS
)
[
57
]

with a flavor of higher-order contracts
[
22
]
.
It seems that, however, the consistency of generated code as to shapes
is not guaranteed by language-level metatheory in this method;
it is not the language (in particular, not the type system)
but programmers who write contracts as to shapes
that are responsible for ensuring such consistency.

9
Conclusion and Future Work

By utilizing staged computation,
we have proposed a method that ensures the consistency as to tensor shapes
through compile-time computation,
aiming at an affinity with continuous development.
We have also offered features
for further reducing the burden of writing tensor-involving programs,
such as implicit parameters or a non-staged surface language.
Various future directions can be considered furthermore,
as some of them are mentioned in Section
8
,
and others are as follows:
(1) support basic type-related devices such as polymorphism or algebraic datatypes;
(2) generalize
\lambda^{\langle\rangle(\!\!\!\;||\!\!\!\;)}
to a multi-stage version
and inspect the relationship between that language and

\lambda^{\mathrm{MD}}

[
42
]
;
(3) improve elaboration rules so that
fewer terms will be duplicated through assertion insertion; and
(4) investigate the interoperability of our method with
programs written in Idris or some dependently-typed languages.

Appendix B
Notes on the Inference of Implicit Arguments

This section briefly discusses the sensitiveness of the inference algorithm
to the description of types.
As we have seen in Section
7
,
the function
Tensor.cross_entropy_for_logits

has the following interface:

⬇

val

~
gen_cross_entropy_for_logits

:

{
s

:

{
v

:

List

Nat

|

List
.
length

v

==

2}}

->

&(
Tensor

%
s

->

Tensor

%[
List
.
nth

0

s
]

->

Tensor

%[])

external

...

Apparently, this looks equivalent to the following:

⬇

val

~
gen_cross_entropy_for_logits

:

{
m

:

Nat
}

->

{
n

:

Nat
}

->

&(
Tensor

%[
m
,

n
]

->

Tensor

%[
m
]

->

Tensor

%[])

external

...

However, the former is actually easier to handle than the latter
in terms of the inference of implicit arguments.
For example, consider checking
the application
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\sim}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\text{{\small{gen\_cross\_entropy\_for\_logits}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}M^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
.
If we use the former interface, we can infer that
the argument corresponding to the parameter
s

can be
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
, simply looking at the type
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\mathtt{Tensor}}\ {\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\%}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

of the first runtime argument
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}M^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
.
Precisely speaking, the reconstructed argument should be
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is a cast used to confirm that

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
is certainly a list of exactly two natural numbers.
Things become a bit more complicated when using the latter;
matching
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
against the “pattern”
[m, n]
,
we can deduce that the arguments corresponding to

m
and

n
can be

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\text{{\small{List.nth}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathtt{0}}\ \mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}
and

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\text{{\small{List.nth}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathtt{1}}\ \mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}
, respectively.

The current implementation of our prototype type-checker is, however,
not wise enough to handle the latter in the manner explained above.
This is simply because it did not need to be so ingenious;
we can basically avoid interfaces like the latter.
Using the latter interface of
Tensor.cross_entropy_for_logits

to type-check the example program
mnist/linear.hrs

(which is displayed on Figure
10
)
indeed results in the following error:

⬇

Cannot

infer

an

implicit

argument

for

n

(
line

9,

columns

4-35)

Tensor
.
cross_entropy_for_logits

^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

application

context
:

_
,

Tensor

%(
BROADCAST

[
num_train_images
,

label_count
]

[
label_count
]),

Vec

%
num_train_images

type
:

{
n

:

{
Int

|

<=

0}}

->

&(
Mat

%
m

%
n

->

Vec

%
m

->

Tensor

%[])

That is, matching the expression
broadcast [num_train_images, label_count] [label_count]

against
[m, n]
failed
(Recall:
Mat %m %n
is a shorthand for
Tensor %[m, n]
).

Figure 18:
The (declarative) rules for binding-time analysis

Figure
18
describes the declarative BTA rules
by using
\hat{A}
and
\mathit{\Delta}
defined as follows:

\displaystyle\hat{A}

\displaystyle\ \mathrel{::=}\ {A^{b}}

\displaystyle A

\displaystyle\ \mathrel{::=}\ {\mathbf{base}}\ \mid\ {\hat{A}\to\hat{A}}\ \mid\ {\{\hat{A}\}\to\hat{A}}

\displaystyle\mathit{\Delta}

\displaystyle\ \mathrel{::=}\ {\bullet}\ \mid\ {\mathit{\Delta},x:\hat{A}\mathbin{@}b}

Type-like entities
\hat{A}
are basically “skeletons” of usual types
where each subpart is equipped with a binding time;
they represent only the structure of functions.
The judgment
\mathit{\Delta}\vdash E:\hat{A}\rightsquigarrow\hat{e}
can be read
“under
\mathit{\Delta}
, the expression
E
is assigned
\hat{A}

and elaborates to
\hat{e}
.”

Let us look through some rules in Figure
18
.
First,
AE-AbsOpt
and
AE-AppOpt
translate
abstractions and applications for implicit parameters/arguments, respectively.
Because implicit parameters/arguments must be at stage
0

in the target language
\lambda^{\langle\rangle(\!\!\!\;||\!\!\!\;)\{\}}
,
these rules require the binding time of elaborated expressions to be
0
.
Guided by the binding time of the function,
AE-App
inserts holes
\_

for the positions where omitted arguments should be completed.
Since arguments can be elided at other positions than the function part of applications,
this rule does not support all the possible cases of omission,
but this is sufficient to cover most of the typical use cases.

AE-Abs
translates type annotations for binders
by the judgment
\mathit{\Delta}\vdash T_{{\mathrm{1}}}\rightsquigarrow A_{{\mathrm{1}}}^{b_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mid\hat{\tau}_{{\mathrm{1}}}
.

AE-Cst0
and
AE-CstP
check constants
by using the map
\mathcal{D}\colon d\mapsto({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}p}\mid c)
,
which associates each constant in Horsea
with the corresponding one in
\lambda^{\langle\rangle(\!\!\!\;||\!\!\!\;)\{\}}
, and
the conversions
\lceil{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathcal{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\rceil_{0}=\hat{A}
,
\lceil{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\rceil_{1}=\hat{A}
,
and
\lceil b,{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\rceil=\hat{A}
,
which extract binding-time types from staged types.

AT-Tensor2
is the most essential rule for this conversion.
It requires argument expressions of tensor types to be at stage
0

and tensor types themselves to be at stage
1
.
Another characteristic case is about function types:

AT-Arr
and
AT-ArrNonDep
.
The restrictions
b\leq b_{{\mathrm{1}}}
and
b\leq b_{{\mathrm{2}}}
imposed by
AT-ArrNonDep

come from a line of previous studies about partial evaluation
[
51
,
29
,
3
]
;
these intuitively state that
values passed to or returned by a function must be available at runtime
if the function is available at runtime.
These two also apply to
AT-Arr
, but
since dependent function types can only be used at stage-
0
in the target language,
they are assigned
b:=0
, and thus the restrictions trivially hold.

The BTA rules introduced in this section are
basically a natural extension of those in the literature,
but there is one interesting point:
while we must be careful about
whether each
\lambda
-abstraction will have a dependent function type
so that we can properly judge binding times,
we do not have to track dependent type-like entities through the analysis;
using
\hat{A}
suffices.
This can be explained intuitively like the following:
Suppose
(\lambda x:T_{{\mathrm{1}}}.\ E_{{\mathrm{2}}})
will have
an essentially dependent function type
\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}S^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}S^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}

after BTA and thereby
we must judge beforehand that this
\lambda
-abstraction be at stage
0
.
Since
x
occurs in
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}S^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
,
x
must have occurred in
E_{{\mathrm{2}}}
as well.
This occurrence will generate some constraint that forces the binding time of
x
to be
0
.
Therefore, we do not have to track the occurrence of
x
in types
to judge whether the
\lambda
-abstraction must reside at stage
0
or not.

Figure 21:
Insertion of staging constructs by using binding times

Lastly, we touch on how to “implement” the binding-time analysis.
The rules for the judgment
\mathit{\Delta}\vdash E:\hat{A}\rightsquigarrow\hat{e}
are declarative
in the sense that each binding times cannot be obtained in a syntax-directed traversal.
For actual implementation,
we have to use an algorithmic version
\mathit{\Delta}\vdash E:\hat{A}\rightsquigarrow\hat{e}\mid C
,
where
C
ranges over the set of finite sets of constraints
of the form
b_{{\mathrm{1}}}=b_{{\mathrm{2}}}
or
b_{{\mathrm{1}}}\leq b_{{\mathrm{2}}}
,
and binding times
b
are extended with
binding-time variables

\beta

(i.e.,
b\ \mathrel{::=}\ {0}\ \mid\ {1}\ \mid\ {\beta}
).
The derivation rules generate
constraints
C
on binding-time variables through traversal
to solve them afterwards, just as the standard Hindley—Milner type inference
[
36
,
50
]

does by tracking types containing type variables.
Figures
19
and
20

describe these rules and the subsequent constraint-solving algorithm, respectively.
Note that solutions are not necessarily unique;
some variables can remain unresolved.
One can substitute such variables with either
0
or
1
.

Miscellaneous rules for correctness proof

For simplicity, we assume the so-called
Barendregt convention
henceforth,
i.e., by appropriate
\alpha
-renaming, we can assume w.l.o.g.
that no variable names are bound more than once in a scope.
As mentioned in Section
3.2
,
we also assume the following:

Assumption 8

(Consistency of Built-in Constants)
.

1.

For each
c
, we have a natural number
\mathop{\mathrm{ar}}(c)
called
the arity of
c
.

2.

For each
c
, its type
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}:=\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c)
is a first-order type,
i.e., there exist
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and a sequence
({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{i}}})_{i=1}^{m}
,
where
m:=\mathop{\mathrm{ar}}(c)
, such that:

•

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}\cdots\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{m}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,

•

\vdash^{1}_{\mathrm{oz}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{i}}}
for each
i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}
, and

•

\vdash^{1}_{\mathrm{oz}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

For a function
c
of arity

and a sequence
(c_{\mathit{i}})_{i=1}^{m}

\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c_{\mathit{i}})={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{i}}}

\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c)=:{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}\cdots\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{m}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
there exists

such that

\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c},({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{\mathit{i}}})_{i=1}^{m})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c^{\prime}}

and
\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c^{\prime})={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

4.

If
\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c},({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{\mathit{i}}})_{i=1}^{k})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}

, and

•

there exist a sequence
({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{i}}})_{i=1}^{k}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that:

–

\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c)={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}\cdots\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{k}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
, and

–

\mathcal{B}_{\%}(c_{\mathit{i}})={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{i}}}
for each

For each
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}p}

Lemma 10

(Substitution)
.

Suppose
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.
We have the following (under the Barendregt convention):

1.

If
\mathit{\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}:({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{0},\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

\mathit{\Gamma},[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

If
\mathit{\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}:({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{0},\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}:{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
then
\mathit{\Gamma},[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{1}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}:[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

If
\mathit{\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}:({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{0},\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
then
\mathit{\Gamma},[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

4.

If

,
then
\mathit{\Gamma},[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}\vdash^{1}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

5.

If
\vdash\mathit{\Gamma},{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}:({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{0},\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}

then
\vdash\mathit{\Gamma},[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathit{\Gamma}^{\prime}

Proof.

Lemma 11

(Target typing synthesizes only well-formed types)
.

1.

\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
implies
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

Theorem
1

(Soundness of Assertion Insertion)
.

Suppose
\vdash\mathit{\Gamma}
.

1.

If
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}M^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\rightsquigarrow{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}:{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

D.2
Preservation and Progress

Lemma 12

(Reduction conforms to CSR equivalence)
.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\equiv^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By straightforward induction on the derivation.
∎

Corollary 13
.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\equiv^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By straightforward induction on the length of the reduction sequence.
∎

Lemma 22

(CSR equivalence preserves unlifting relation)
.

\gg

Lemma 32
.

If
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\gg{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

Proof.

By induction on the derivation of
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

•

Case

T0-CstP

T0-RfnPred
:
Since

Case

Lemma 33

(Determinism of
\longrightarrow
)
.

1.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, then
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

2.

If
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, then
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

3.

If
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, then
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

Proof.

By straightforward mutual induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
, and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.
∎

Lemma 34
.

Suppose that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is a closed term and is not a value.

1.

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

2.

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}p}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}p}
.

3.

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}
.

Proof.

1.

By case analysis on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c^{\prime}}
:
Since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c^{\prime}}
,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c^{\prime}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
, which finishes the proof.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
:
Since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.
However, this contradicts the assumption
because
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is assumed not to be a value
while
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
is.

•

The other cases clearly contradict the assumption.

2.

Can be proved in the same manner as (1).

3.

By induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
Immediate from (1).

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}p}
:
This is also immediate from (2).

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
:
We do the following case analysis on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
:

–

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
:
This contradicts the assumption that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is not a value
since we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.

–

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
:
This contradicts the assumption by

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}
.

–

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
:
We have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}

and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.
By IH, we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
,
and by (1), we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.
Therefore, we have

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}
.

–

The other cases clearly contradict
the assumption
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

∎

is a value.

Lemma 36
.

Suppose that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
are closed terms
and that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
,
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
are all values.
If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
, then
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

Proof.

By case analysis on
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
:

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}=\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\lambda}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{11}}}}\mathpunct{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}.}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}
:
We have only the following derivation for

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
assuming
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
w.l.o.g. by the Barendregt convention:

\displaystyle\frac{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\end{array}}{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\lambda}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{11}}}}\mathpunct{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}.}}\ [{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\ \mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}[[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}][{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}\end{array}}

E0-Beta
.

We will show that

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathrel{:=}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}

satisfies the desired properties.
First, we have

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}][{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}][{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.
Then,
since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
is a value while
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
is not,

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
is a value by Lemma
35
.
Therefore,
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
is clearly a value,
and we can derive
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

as follows:

\displaystyle\frac{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\end{array}}{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\lambda}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{11}}}}\mathpunct{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}.}}\ [{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\ \mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}[[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}][{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{12}}}}\end{array}}

E0-Beta
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
:
Since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
,
we have the following as the sole derivation of

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
:

\displaystyle\frac{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}\end{array}}{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}\end{array}}

E0-Delta
.

We will show that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathrel{:=}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}
satisfies the desired properties.
First, by
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}

and Lemma
34
,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.
Since we have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}

and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
,
we can immediately derive

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{B}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

as follows:

\displaystyle\frac{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}})={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}\end{array}}{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}\end{array}}

E0-Delta
.

Also, we clearly have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}q}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}v^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}=\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(\!\!\!\;|}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\triangleleft}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\nu}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}B}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mid}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{11}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}|\!)}}^{L}

Lemma 37

(Bisimulation on essential reductions of applications)
.

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
,
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
are all values.

1.

Left-hand side:
If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
, then
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

Right-hand side:
If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
, then
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\longrightarrow^{0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

Proof.

Since
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
is also a value by Lemma

Therefore, we can prove (1) and (2) as follows:

1.

We can finish by Lemma

(where

We can finish by Lemma

(where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N_{\mathrm{A}}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathrel{:=}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}

Lemma 38

(Weak bisimulation, left-hand side)
.

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.

1.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

3.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

Proof.

By mutual induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

1.

•

Case

Lemma 39
.

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.

1.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
is a stage-
0
value,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

(A)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,

(B)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
is a stage-
0
value, and

(C)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
is a stage-
1
value,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

(A)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,

(B)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
is a stage-
1
value, and

(C)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathrel{=:}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
is a type value, then

(X)

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
, and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
:

1.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
:
We will show that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathrel{:=}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
satisfies the desired properties.
First, since
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is a closed term by
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
,
we have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.
Therefore, we have (A) by
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.
Also, (B) immediately holds by the assumption that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
is a stage-
0
value.
Finally, we have (C) by
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}
such that
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x^{\prime}}\neq{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
:
This contradicts the assumption that
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}(}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0})}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

∎

Lemma 40

(Weak bisimulation, right-hand side)
.

Suppose
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.

1.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{N}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

If
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{T}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By mutual induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
, and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

similar to the one for Lemma
38
(i.e. the left-hand side version).

1.

Lemma 41

(One-step, one-variable cotermination)
.

1.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

2.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

Proof.

1.

By induction on the number of steps of
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

•

Case
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
We have the following two cases:

–

Case where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
This contradicts the assumption
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

–

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
We clearly have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

•

Case where there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
By Lemma
38
,
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
such that

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.
Then, by IH on
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
which has a strictly shorter evaluation sequence,
we have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.
Therefore, we have

[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{\ast\,0}[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

2.

By induction on the number of steps of
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

•

Case
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
We have the following two cases:

–

Case where
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
and
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
:
Since
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
we clearly have
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}

Lemma 42

(One-variable cotermination)
.

1.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

2.

If
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
and
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
[{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}/{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}]{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

Proof.

By induction on the number of steps of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}

using Lemma
41
.
∎

Lemma 43

(Cotermination)
.

1.

If
\sigma_{{\mathrm{1}}}\longrightarrow\sigma_{{\mathrm{2}}}
and
\sigma_{{\mathrm{1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
\sigma_{{\mathrm{2}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

2.

If
\sigma_{{\mathrm{1}}}\longrightarrow\sigma_{{\mathrm{2}}}
and
\sigma_{{\mathrm{2}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
,
then
\sigma_{{\mathrm{1}}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}
.

Proof.

By induction on the size of
\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\sigma_{{\mathrm{1}}}
using Lemma
42
.
∎

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\gg{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

Proof.

By induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}B}
:
We have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\equiv^{0}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\nu}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}B}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mid}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathtt{true}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\}}}
,
and by Lemma
18
,

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
is of the form
\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\nu}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}B}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mid}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\}}}
.
Thus, we have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\gg{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

•

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\mathtt{Tensor}}\ {\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\%}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}s}
:
We have
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\equiv^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathtt{Tensor}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}s}
,
and by Lemma
19
,

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\mathtt{Tensor}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}s}
.
Therefore, we have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\gg{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\equiv^{0}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}\mathop{\downarrow}({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}})\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\to}}\mathop{\downarrow}({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}})

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}

Lemma 55

(Progress by
\delta
-reduction of persistent built-in functions)
.

If
\mathit{\Gamma}\vdash^{0}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{c}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\ \cdots\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{\mathit{m}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}:{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

,
then there exists
c
such that

\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{c}},({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{1}}}},\ldots,{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{\mathit{m}}}))={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c^{\prime}}
.

\mathcal{B}_{\%}(\hat{c})\mathrel{=:}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{\tau}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}\cdots\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{\tau}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{\mathit{m}}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\to}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\hat{\tau}^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

with

for each

.
Then, by Assumption
8
,
there exists
c
such that

\delta({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\hat{c}},({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{{\mathrm{1}}}},\ldots,{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c_{\mathit{m}}}))={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}c}

Lemma 57

(Reduction conforms to
\beta
-equivalence)
.

1.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\cong^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\cong^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\cong^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By straightforward induction on the derivation.
∎

Lemma 58
.

1.

\sigma\longrightarrow\sigma^{\prime}
implies
\sigma{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\cong^{0}\sigma^{\prime}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
.

2.

\sigma\longrightarrow\sigma^{\prime}
implies
\sigma{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\cong^{1}\sigma^{\prime}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

3.

\sigma\longrightarrow\sigma^{\prime}
implies

\sigma\longrightarrow\sigma^{\prime}
implies
\sigma{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\cong^{1}\sigma^{\prime}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}

Proof.

By mutual induction on the structure of
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

1.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}

–

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\in\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\sigma=\mathop{\mathrm{dom}}\sigma^{\prime}

,
we have

,
we have

.

–

we can immediately finish the proof by

\displaystyle\frac{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}\end{array}}{\begin{array}[]{@{}c@{}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\cong^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\end{array}}

.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\lambda}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\mathpunct{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}.}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8})}}

\Longrightarrow^{0}

Lemma 68
.

For any value of the form
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}
,

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}\Longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}a}

Lemma 70
.

If
\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(\!\!\!\;|}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\triangleleft}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}|\!)}}^{L}\Longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
, then we have
one of the following:

1.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}=\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(\!\!\!\;|}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\triangleleft}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}|\!)}}^{L}
, or

2.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}={\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\lambda}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}:}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathpunct{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}.}}\ {\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
for some
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}x}
.

Proof.

By tracing back the derivation of
\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}(\!\!\!\;|}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathrel{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\triangleleft}}\mathopen{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\langle}}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}\rangle}}\mathclose{{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}|\!)}}^{L}\Longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
we have the following two cases:

Lemma 71

(Substitution preserves parallel reduction)
.

Lemma 73

(Confluence by conversion à la Takahashi)
.

1.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\Longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\Longrightarrow^{0}({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{\ast}
.

2.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}})^{\ast}
.

3.

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\Longrightarrow^{0}{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}\Longrightarrow^{0}({\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}})^{\ast}
.

4.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}({\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}})^{\ast}
.

Proof.

By mutual induction on the structure of

{\color[rgb]{0,0.4,0.8}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(0)}}
,
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}N^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,

Corollary 74

(Confluence)
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

Immediate from Lemma
73
.
∎

Lemma 75

(Church—Rosser)
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
,
then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By repeated use of Corollary
74
.
∎

Lemma 76
.

If
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longleftrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, then there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By induction on the “length” of
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longleftrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
:
Immediate by Lemma
61
.

•

Case where there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longleftrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
:
By IH on
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longleftrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
, which is a “strictly shorter” sequence,
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.
By transitivity, from
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
we also have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

•

Case where there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longleftrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
:
Similarly to the previous case, by IH, there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
.
Then, by Lemma
75
,
from
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
,
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.
By transitivity, from
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{0}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
we also have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

∎

Lemma 78
.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

Proof.

By induction on the “length” of
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

•

Case
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
is immediate.

•

Case where
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
for some
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
:
By
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and Lemma
69
,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
. Therefore, by IH on
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
,
which is a “strictly shorter” reduction sequence,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.

∎

Lemma 79
.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\cong^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
implies
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.

Proof.

By
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\cong^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
and Corollary
77
,
there exists
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
such that

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
and
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}\Longrightarrow^{1\,\ast}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}
.
Therefore, by Lemma
78
,
we have
{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}T^{\prime\scriptscriptstyle(1)}}={\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
.
∎

Lemma
5
.

{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{1}}}}\equiv^{1}{\color[rgb]{0.7,0.3,0}\tau^{\scriptscriptstyle(1)}_{{\mathrm{2}}}}
